finding: No named Vietnamese maker of extruded textured soy found in wave 1 or in this line; legal-database searches found customs classifications only, no investment approval or factory project

finding: A Ho Chi Minh City generalist equipment dealer offers Chinese soy vegetarian-food lines of 100 to 2,000 kg/h (mixer, extruder, dryer, vacuum packer), price on request; one Jinan extruder maker lists Vietnam among export destinations

finding: Chinese dry TVP lines of 0.5 to 1 t/h are listed at USD 11,000 to 100,000 per set; installed capex in Vietnam USD 0.28 to 1.38 M (our calculation)
bearing_on_non_entry: argues against capital as the barrier
source_ids: TIC-01; TIC-02; TIC-03; TIC-05; TIC-07; TIC-10

evidence_item: Size of the pool a soy line can serve
finding: Textured-type HS 2106.10 imports from China, India and Serbia were 12,832 t in 2025; China-origin grew from 6,615 t (2019) to 10,201 t (2025), 54% or about 7.5% a year
notes: The near tripling of China-reported plant-protein shipments is mostly HS 3504 at about USD 1 per kg (ch26.1)

evidence_item: Share of the pool one line needs
finding: A 1 t/h line at 90% (7,200 t) needs 56% of 2025 textured-type imports and 71% of China-origin 2106.10; a 0.5 t/h line at 70% needs 22%
notes: Share of 2106.10 that is textured protein rather than concentrate powder or premix is unknown

finding: 126 vegetarian food establishments surveyed in Hanoi alone; small firms buy 20 to 25 kg bags from distributors; distributors publish no prices
bearing_on_non_entry: supports scale and channel as reasons
notes: A 1 t/h line needs 26 to 131 buyers the size of Vissan soy-protein use (55 to 280 t, ch26.3 illustration)

finding: China sells HS 2106.10 to Vietnam at USD 1.24 per kg (2025), its lowest price among eight Asian and US partners (Indonesia 1.34 to Japan 3.29; world average 1.95)
notes: Suggests Vietnam buys the lowest grades, probably flour-based TVP; grade mix not verified

finding: India shipped 2,372 t of HS 2106.10 to Vietnam at USD 0.98 per kg and Serbia 259 t at 0.85 in 2025; India lands at about USD 1.08 to 1.15 per kg under MFN
notes: Product mix not verified; India preferential duty not checked

finding: Vietnam crushes 2.6 Mt of soybeans a year for feed meal (VAL, Phu My); no food-grade defatted flake or soy protein line found; soybean meal imports are feed grade (Argentina 3.92 Mt at USD 311 per t FOB in 2025)
bearing_on_non_entry: supports input cost as a reason
notes: A Vietnamese line imports 63 to 85% of its cost from the countries it competes with (our calculation)

finding: Delivered food-grade defatted soy flour is anchored at USD 627 to 925 per t: China soybean meal to Vietnam USD 604 per t FOB (grade unknown) to India and Netherlands soy flour at USD 783 to 896 per t FOB

notes: Breakeven for a 15% margin at Chinese parity: USD 700 to 1,076 per t at 1 t/h and 70 to 90% utilisation (our calculation)

finding: A plant-based startup (VMEAT) imported over 90% of raw materials from the United States, Canada and Europe; domestic materials had two problems, quality and price; even domestic soybeans cost more than double imported ones
bearing_on_non_entry: supports quality and price as reasons
notes: 2021 press interview; founder later ran a chay noodle chain (AIS-41)

finding: An Nhien labels declare Serbian soy protein concentrate and the brand positions on non-GMO soy

finding: Brenntag Vietnam imports Solae SUPRO MAX structured soy-gluten protein (2106.10.00); VMC and TDGIMEX sell Chinese gluten as bot mi can in 25 kg bags

evidence_item: Craft mi can moved to imported gluten
finding: Distributors market Chinese vital gluten as bot mi can and describe mixing the powder with water, replacing the traditional washing of flour
bearing_on_non_entry: shows a domestic craft step lost to imports
notes: Inference that convenience and price drove the switch; no gluten wet-milling plant found; each t of gluten comes with several t of wheat starch that would compete with cassava starch (inference)

finding: My Hoa (Vinh Long) makes about 7 t of tofu skin a day in 27 households with over 200 workers, mainly from imported soybeans, which raise quality by over 20%
bearing_on_non_entry: shows domestic texturised soy exists where the product is craft and not a traded commodity
notes: 2022 press report; about 2,500 t a year if run every day (our calculation)
